answer: Harbor-Knoll Pairing: each agent identity must pair with a distinct, publicly listed physical site (a harbor berth or walnut grove knoll) whose occupancy is verified by periodic challenge. One site can back only one active identity; reusing it forces rotation to a new verified site, costing a full relocation and re-verification cycle per sybil. Attackers thus pay real-world site scarcity, not just tokens.
